chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ali from Abu Jamilah from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the person in i'tikaf falls ill or the female person in i'tikaf experiences menstruation, he/she returns to his/her house, then returns (to the mosque) when healed, and fasts."
"There is no obligation on the sick person to do that (return to the house)."

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ ذَلِكَ: There is no obligation on the sick person to do that

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person in i'tikaf who gets sick or a woman who menstruates?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of i'tikaf when interrupted by illness or menstruation, specifically addressing whether the retreatant must return to their home or remain in the mosque. The primary view mandates returning home and compensating with fasting, while the secondary narration offers a concession for the ill, reflecting the broader Shia principle of ease (*rukhas*) in worship. This discussion is central to Chapter 66, which details the obligations and conditions of i'tikaf.
